name: DAO Maker Vesting
rootCause: DAO Maker issued an announcement stating that at around 1:00 UTC on August 12th, hackers maliciously used a DAO Maker wallet and obtained administrator rights. After initially testing this vulnerability and successfully stealing 10,000 USDC, the cybercriminal made another 15 transactions quietly. In this way, hackers embezzled approximately $7 million before the security team was able to track, control, and prevent the outflow of funds. A total of 5,251 users were affected, and each user lost an average of $1250. Fortunately, users who hold up to $900 in funds are not affected at all.

descriptions.text: DAO Maker issued an announcement stating that at around 1:00 UTC on August 12th, hackers maliciously used a DAO Maker wallet and obtained administrator rights. After initially testing this vulnerability and successfully stealing 10,000 USDC, the cybercriminal made another 15 transactions quietly. In this way, hackers embezzled approximately $7 million before the security team was able to track, control, and prevent the outflow of funds. A total of 5,251 users were affected, and each user lost an average of $1250. Fortunately, users who hold up to $900 in funds are not affected at all.

An attacker exploited a re-invokable init() function in DAO Maker's Ethereum vesting contracts in early September 2021, seizing ownership and draining user funds through privileged withdrawals. Loss estimates range from $4M to $7M, affecting over 5,000 accounts. The vulnerability stemmed from unguarded initialization logic in upgradeable contracts. DAO Maker's vesting contracts allowed the init() function to be called multiple times after deployment, enabling an attacker to reassign ownership and invoke privileged withdrawal functions without restriction. No single-call guard or access control protected contract initialization.
